subject: Archaeology
title: The Roman Sewer: Cloaca Maxima
description: One-minute skill: The Roman Sewer: Cloaca Maxima.

hook.text: Rome's greatest engineering feat might not be the Colosseum. It might be the sewer built in 600 BCE.

buildup.text: The Cloaca Maxima drained the swampy Forum and channeled waste into the Tiber River through stone tunnels.

discovery.text: At its widest, the tunnel is large enough for a horse and cart. It was big enough to serve a city of one million.

twist.text: The sewer is still part of Rome's drainage system today — 2,600 years old and still functioning.

climax.text: The goddess Cloacina was the patron of the sewer. Romans worshipped their plumbing — literally.

punchline.text: Romans built a sewer, worshipped it, and it outlasted their empire.

quiz.question: What is remarkable about the Cloaca Maxima?
options: It was the first sewer to use ceramic pipes
It is still part of Rome's drainage system after 2,600 years
It was large enough to serve as an underground road during floods
